mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior quarter's median triggers a risk-off sentiment that compresses equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its prior quarter median by at least 25 bps
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar tightening episodes are not statistically lower than in pre-tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three consecutive months signal disinflation, which reduces market expectations for future inflation and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls for three consecutive months below the prior month's value
failure_condition: Overlapping 20-day forward returns during similar disinflation episodes do not outperform a neutral benchmark (mean of -0.1%).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs surprises to the upside and boosts consumer confidence, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 by at least 20,000 jobs in a single month
failure_condition: In 5 prior similar labor expansions, 20-day forward returns did not exceed +0.5% in 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below the prior quarter's median, accompanied by a decline in housing starts (HOUST), predicts a supply-side shock that depresses equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below prior quarter median AND HOUST falls by at least 10% from prior quarter median
failure_condition: During comparable supply shocks, the 20-day forward return was not more than -1.0% in 80% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) growth above 3% suggests accelerating economic activity, which raises growth expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO grows at a monthly rate exceeding 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 10 prior expansionary INDPRO accelerations, 60-day forward returns were not statistically higher than in neutral periods (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% triggers a policy tightening anticipation effect, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% in a single month
failure_condition: During comparable UNRATE declines, 20-day forward returns were not more negative than -0.2% in 70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in retail sales proxy (not available in provided catalog; fallback: use RSAFS as a proxy for consumer demand) of 5% or more for two consecutive months signals weakening demand, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls for two consecutive months by at least 5% from prior month
failure_condition: In analogous demand weakness episodes (using RSAFS), 20-day forward returns were not more negative than -0.3% in 80% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a prolonged period of declining inflation (CPIAUCSL falling for four consecutive months below 3%) combined with a flat or rising FEDFUNDS rate suggests the Fed is holding policy steady, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls for four consecutive months below 3% AND FEDFUNDS does not rise by more than 1 bps over the same period
failure_condition: In prior neutral-to-loose inflation windows, 60-day forward returns did not outperform a 0% baseline by more than +0.5% in 50% of cases.
